newsitem.title: USA: Sierra sees merger accretive in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Sierra sees merger accretive in 1997.

text.p: Sierra Health Services Inc Chairman Anthony Marlon Wednesday said he expected the company's planned purchase of Physician Corp of America to be accretive to its earnings in 1997.
"There has been some confusion over whether the synergies make this deal accretive to earnings," said Anothony Marlon, who added, "They do."
He said he saw benefits of $15 million from the combination of the two health-care providers. "If you give me credit for only 60 percent of those synergies, the deal is accretive," he added.

Marlon was responding to Wall Street's chilly response on Monday to news of the merger agreement. Sierra's share price fell as several analysts lowered their ratings on the stock, citing expectations that the merger would be dilutive, among other reasons.
On Wednesday, Sierra's stock recovered much of its lost ground and were trading up 3-3/4 to 27 late in the day.
"There will be minor dilution in the second and third quarter, becoming significantly accretive in the fourth quarter and the full year," said Marlon.
He said his forecast was based partly on a belief that analysts' estimates that Physician Corp would earn about $0.80 per share next year were too low.
"We believe, based on our due diligence over the last 90 days, that they will earn between $1.04 and $1.05 per share on a stand-alone basis," Marlon said.

"We believe that Physican Corp has certain assets that are performing reasonably well in Puerto Rico and Texas, and we believe their Florida assets need significant work, and we are prepared to undertake that work," he added.
